regions.brief: Terraced frontier settlement on the west cliff; the east road is the only public entrance to the sanctuary. Main street is broad and safe. Orphanage hill is reached by two short flights of steps, with a return street descending to the guild. The workshop is outdoors beneath an awning; practice targets face a stone backstop. Build the skyline before the interior spaces. Use warm clay, bronze, cloth and mossy stone. No combat, no secret boss, no mandatory currency grind. The release ceremony shows an Echo departing before any energy tutorial. Mira's orphanage has ordinary toys, laundry and a handrail at child height. Copperwings perch on roof ridges, lantern moths cluster around flowers; town NPCs move short loops rather than blocking the player. After Warp, the surface is unreachable, not destroyed; exterior remains a historical map landmark.

regions.brief: A broad open-air foothill valley between the town and the sanctuary rim. The path descends to a shallow brook, then rises along a ruined aqueduct; its broken span is supported by stone piers and accessible lower recovery deck. The bell tower is visible from two distinct elevations. No deep-water swimming; fish are in a background stream or below a traversable bank. Tall grass in foreground is faded near Aster. Tutorial Forager patrols a flat clearing with a retreat route, no offscreen attack. Introduce jump and dodge in separate low-risk stretches. Use grass-top edges, dirt interior, exposed rock corner, fallen pale-alloy conduit; the path blends to cut stone over 6–10 tiles. Copperwings, Bristle Hares, Lantern Moths and Ribbonfish establish normal ecology. After Warp the entrance to town is blocked at the cut corridor; the surviving wilds remain revisitable.

regions.brief: A ridgeline of wooden hunting platforms wrapped around stone spires, not a straight corridor. Split Walk forks into an upper birdwatching hide, a lower canopy trail and the main ridge. Skyhunt Tower is a viewpoint reached by staggered walkable ledges, not a new jump power. Trigger the Warp only after the player is safely beyond the cut point at Fracture Crossing: freeze input briefly for the authored scene, restore control on a stable ledge, permanently close the town route, and open the camp descent. On return the player sees broken ropes and a missing distant vista; surface communication fails. Foragers patrol ground and Rift Skitters appear only after the event. Steam vents are old human field equipment and visibly warn. Bristle Hares retreat to brush, Copperwings scatter on first shock; no repeated cutscene. Place map clue tags near branch points, not floating in empty air.

regions.brief: A small expedition site tucked beneath the hunter ridge. Broken guy ropes, weathered tents and overturned diagnostic stands tell the story of a hurried evacuation. The main path descends from the shelter to the tent and a survey overlook. An optional high ledge holds a torn pack and has a return ramp; do not force climbing the whole ridge again. The restored map reveals an old public-maintenance passage west across the head of the valley. The gate is a mechanical route barrier, not a blank wall. P02 uses bell, split rock and camp arch as three actual visible landmarks. Keep orientation consistent across the overworld and journal. Minimal combat: one Forager patrol outside the shelter, no enemy interrupting the map UI. Rainwater drips into pans, a Copperwing may land after the Warp settles; the camp is quiet rather than fully dead.

regions.brief: This is the hydraulic control head of the sanctuary: gravity-fed catchment above the valves, pressure gallery below, water falling toward the garden and Echo Reservoir. Build huge arches, damp steps, a dry spillway and giant bronze wheel with a clearly walkable rim. P01 controls are geographically separated along the feeder circuit, yet all within a compact loop; walk between Root Arch, Bell Feeder and Split Stone. The final regulator displays the sequence; incorrect input clears only the command buffer, not the route or collectibles. Root Arch and Bell symbols correspond to landmarks; a relief says Root before Bell; a damaged plinth says center Split Stone last. Warden stands astride the outlet bridge, uses slams and exposed arm; bridge raises on correct flow, safe-mode unlocks exit on defeat. Spillway ladder shortcut opens after local latch; no early Warden bypass. Sluice Swifts shelter in eaves, glassfin fish and crabs appear when water resumes. No collision on decorative falling water. Pressure machinery uses visible gauge and audible warning.

regions.brief: The Great Root dominates the middle of the map. Design three playable elevations: canopy branches, trunk/terrace network and underroot water service route. The root silhouette is visible from the sluice and archive balcony. Crown Fork is an early optional overlook from Hunter's Reach, but the lower bridge remains disconnected until Warden is defeated. The main route crosses Root Bridge and follows root stair terraces to Foundry Footbridge. Garden branch curves below the bridge; water is dry before Sluice and remains isolated until M06 connects the garden valve. After restoration, fish appear, pond lilies open, a float platform rises and a return path opens to Sluice. Moss Hollow is a naturally enclosed root cavity, with Titan only after Warden and local marker. No mandatory swimming, swinging, double jump or wall climbing; use broad branch tops and authored ladders or mechanical lifts. Hares, mossback grazers, moths, Copperwings, glassfin shoals, crabs and eels occupy separate habitats. Predators are not background loot. Foreground leaves frame the canopy, then fade around player and telegraphs.

regions.brief: Old manufacturing and repair facilities built to service relics. The outer wall grows through Rootspan; roots penetrate panels before giving way to dry industrial floors. Main spine is a broad maintenance road, above it a suspended crane rail, below it a nonlethal inspection trench. P03 follows a lit source conduit up to a relay and down to a receiver; isolate dead archive spur. Service doors open from both sides after power returns. Golem Walk introduces armored guards with enough space to flank. Prism beams use one-second warnings and safe niches. A service lift climbs to the optional Storage Loft; restore its relay to open a connection back to canopy. Steam vent platforms are optional hazards with readable timing. No foundry molten floor on the mandatory route; visual furnace behind glass. Vault geckos and dust moths occupy broken wall cavities, no wildlife inside active furnaces. Use Foozle laboratory geometry mixed with pale stone and original Vaelari conduit trim.

regions.brief: A tall archive sunk into the rock below the sluice, reached from the foundry along a high viaduct with water flowing beneath. Build monumental vertical stacks, balconies and an astrolabe-like map frame as a navigation landmark. Main path winds down through Archive Steps, across the display bridge and into the map chamber, then exits along the lower terrace. A short optional upper shelf spur contains an archive lock and a late-game return shaft. P04 requires Receiver → Archive → Anchor, taught by glyphs in previous facilities. Each plate is mounted on the same archive apparatus rather than arbitrary remote buttons. Critical map granted after correct sequence and inspection; no optional archive count. A turret watches a side stair with visible beam line; central map area safe. Dust motes, Vault Geckos in damaged upper niches, no fish or birds in sealed stacks. Muted ivory, bronze, cyan accents; transition gradually toward irregular purple geometry at lower terrace.

regions.brief: A fractured connection zone, not an alternate planet by itself. Establish the same pale-alloy architecture from Survey Vault, then offset its repeating patterns along visible rifts. Three anchor mouths share a compact promenade: diamond pair pulses continuously; split and ring mismatches lead to short nonlethal loops returning to the same hub. P05 chooses the matching diamond. The main fold to Veraya is physically represented by an arch boundary and a distinct map glyph; the planets remain separate. M10 traces the optional anchor loop, but cannot open the Veraya shortcut without P05. Rift Skitters and occasional Fold Stalker are telegraphed; floor cracks warn before striking, no invisible walls. Rift moths cluster only near stable edges; displaced species do not instantly become a new food chain. Use suspended-looking fragments attached by traversable decks, not mandatory midair teleport. A distant view of the Reservoir explains a later service return.

regions.brief: This is physically Veraya, connected only through authored Warp throats. Distinguish modern modular steel and bolted laboratory equipment from underlying seamless Vaelari stone. Atrium opens onto an unfamiliar sky beyond a large broken observation window. Research Gallery has current measuring equipment, a named diagnostic recording without revealing Orion, and two traversable maintenance terraces. Foreign Sky is a quiet vista before the separate return fold to Eldara's memorial network. The optional Annex contains equipment and an interface reference but not the actual replacement component; that remains inaccessible until Orion's story. Prism Beetles in open niches and Silverkites outside windows, no Eldaran fish. Defective sentinels patrol lab floor and telegraph charges; no enemy in rest zone. The return fold is stable and bidirectional after P05, not a usable player teleport power. The late service alcove is visible as a one-sided shutter, not a path to the planet surface.

regions.brief: A memorial garden below the archives; enters from Veraya through a localized return fold across the map, not a literal underground corridor between planets. Pale stone, soft pink blossoms, dry paths and slow-moving light; no ordinary hostile combat on the critical route. The memory theatre uses a residual imprint of an ordinary Vaelari life, followed by Aster's childhood reflection. The player can leave after the short scene or replay the archive, no dialogue choice blocks progress. Optional Shrine is a short loop along engraved names and a recorded impression; match the name to M12. Still Garden returns to the hall via steps. Lantern moths gather at flowers, quiet small birds in open-air terraces, no wildlife in sealed memorial recess. Use open negative space, restrained music and no combat sound over the scene. This should be a pacing break, not a filler traversal section.

regions.brief: A vast, partially open cistern with transparent conduits and a towering release manifold visible from several elevations. Distinguish ordinary hydraulic water from Echo channels: water flows blue-green with ripples; Echo energy travels through sealed luminous conduits; an Echo releases upward as a separate motif. Main path wraps around the basin on tiered inspection decks, never requires swimming. P06 follows source feed to three branches: vault power, release path, already-full storage. Toggle Vault ON, Release ON, Full Storage OFF; show pressure bars and arrows. After success lights stabilize and some Echo-dependent enemies leave; ordinary fish can return in physically connected water only. Colossus occupies an alignment court on a broad platform, attacks from marked folds overhead or behind, fully avoidable before Rewind. Overflow branch is optional; isolate after P06, then open return to Warped Verge from local latch. Basin minnows and filter shrimp are in water behind glass; Echo Leeches near exposed bound Echo accumulations, not fish schools. No player resource expenditure on required switches.

regions.brief: A protected relic complex at the end of the reservoir supply bridge. Symmetrical pale-alloy architecture, clean curved surfaces and restrained gold/cyan highlights distinguish it from hunter technology. Vestibule branches to two visible maintenance isolators left/right of Keeper Court; no extra ability to reach them. Once both are off, Keeper shield cycles expose core. Defeating Keeper opens the relic shrine. P08 verifies Sluice Flow, Survey Archive, Reservoir Release; missing indicator explains missing upstream flag. The relic was a rescue/research continuity tool, not a time machine. Aster installs it on his right forearm; immediately save. Return-Path Terrace is a local safe corridor with pad, authored shutter and latch separated by 16 tiles, exactly one continuous loaded domain; use Rewind within six seconds, switch persists, no arbitrary wall traversal. Local reset restores geometry, ability readiness and minimum EE. No wildlife inside sterile vault; calm hum and maintenance dust. Main lower exit opens after training, not by defeating an optional enemy.

regions.brief: The deepest unstable service tunnels loop under the upper sanctuary. Terrain is layered pale rock and violet fractures, with actual solid routes visually distinct from background fragments. History Landing shows a fragment of Continuum doctrine; another record at Fold Junction names Nalora without revealing the whole catastrophe. The old archive return shaft opens after Rewind training and local latch; return cannot bypass earlier mandatory flags. One-Way Gallery contains an optional shutter pocket for M16 and a safe main bypass. P10 uses three pairs A diamond, B split diamond, C ring: visual halves and rhythmic pulses, errors show mismatch and reset only that pair. NEST is a side spur off Junction, accessible after M14 Rewind exercise; a creature destroys an Echo in the background, reinforcing ethics. Optional Rift Devourer arena is a natural hollow with retreat before engagement and retry after death. No full Warp control, no player teleport. Rift Moths flee unstable cracks, no normal birds or fish here. Sparse effects ensure spatial markers remain legible.

regions.brief: Monumental converging architecture. Three stabilizers are integrated into a single multi-level service viaduct: one on western flank, one up a lift, one on lower deck. The player can visit them in any order via an actual loop and returns to Anchor Control. Restore all three, open safe release line, then energize receiver. Each device has a visual link toward the gate and numbered/shape status on the journal; do not require remembering arbitrary order. Main platforms have solid rails, safe lift landings and marked spatial hazards. Optional Service Niche branches from upper terrace near Last Rest; align a conduit for the Resonator, never required for boss. Last Rest is quiet and near final approach, with safe short retry to Guardian. A huge gate silhouette fills background as alignment completes. Sparse Prism Beetles in outer cracks only, no ordinary flora in active containment. Art switches from fractured chaos to monumental symmetry; violet marks remain in cracks, proving the local repair is partial.

regions.brief: A colossal gate at the farthest edge of the accessible sanctuary, approached through a broad containment court. The Last Custodian is a machine trying to protect the passage, not the trilogy villain. Arena seals only after safe entry; all attack zones are signaled; defeat releases a stored reserve source and opens gate approach. Aster inspects broken remote interface and sees the transit alignment fail; physical destination cannot be reached, no hidden alternative exit. Gate is visibly broken before interaction; journal labels it irreparable by Aster. P12 uses Guardian reserve source, isolate failed transit load, connect beacon and confirm distress packet. Player EE not spent. Beacon unlocks safe Refuge Terrace; Aster sets camp and ending follows. No active combat after the court, no ambient animals in sealed machinery; dust and a few quiet distant lights. End screen offers continue from final refuge with return paths to accessible sanctuary, not an alternative escape; post-credits Orion receives signal. Keep the view of the massive gate from earlier regions consistent.

puzzles.goal_clues: Distributed feeder loop: root relief orders Root Arch before Bell; Split Stone plinth says center last. Three controls can be visited safely and the final regulator displays the command buffer.
puzzles.solution: Operate Root Arch Valve, then Bell Feeder Valve, then Split Stone Regulator. Press commit. If order is wrong clear only the local command buffer; valves remain physically accessible.
puzzles.result: Raises bridge to Warden; local spillway can later be unlocked by M05; water reaches main channels.

puzzles.goal_clues: From the survey board the Hanging Bell is west-northwest (OUT-BELL vicinity); Split Rock is the distinct east-northeast ridge silhouette at atlas (116,29); Camp Arch is the origin. Map Tent sketch records all three.
puzzles.solution: Align bell west-northwest, Split Rock east-northeast, Camp Arch at origin; confirm maintenance link to Echo Sluice.
puzzles.result: Reveals the westbound upper service ridge; mismatch highlights the incorrect landmark. Compass directions supersede old V3 positions.

puzzles.goal_clues: Power maintenance receiver. Wall flow diagram and arrows show source→relay→receiver; blocked archive branch.
puzzles.solution: Connect source to service relay, relay to receiver; leave dead archive branch isolated.
puzzles.result: Door opens to REL03; disconnected receiver icon or overload alarm on mistake.

puzzles.goal_clues: Identify survey archive. Three plates show receiver, archive, anchor symbols; service note requires power before record before route.
puzzles.result: Access SUR03; incorrect order resets plates; critical map automatically recorded on entry.

puzzles.goal_clues: Historical map shows three doors; two unstable anchors pulse irregularly. Current landmarks and anchor shape match stable route.
puzzles.solution: Select continuously pulsing matched diamond; wrong anchor mouths loop to the same junction. No shortcuts to Veraya before TOPOLOGY_ALIGNED.
puzzles.result: WAR03 opens; wrong doors loop safely to WAR02 with mismatched landmark feedback.

puzzles.goal_clues: Power vault and preserve safe release. Source feeds three toggles; storage indicator full.
puzzles.solution: Vault power ON, Release ON, Full storage OFF.
puzzles.result: Reservoir stabilizes, local fauna reduced, arena accessible; full storage alarms, no fatal penalty.

puzzles.goal_clues: Keeper shield fed by paired conductors; diagram marks maintenance isolators.
puzzles.solution: Disable left and right isolators; lock offline for encounter.
puzzles.result: Arena opens and core shield windows become available; wrong panel harmless feedback.

puzzles.goal_clues: Relic vault requires verified Sluice flow, Survey archive and Reservoir release. Three indicators and symbols correspond to earlier systems.
puzzles.solution: Set Sluice=Flow, Survey=Archive, Reservoir=Release; confirm when all three prior flags true.
puzzles.result: Relic installed, save immediately; missing inputs identify exact system. Keeper already defeated.

puzzles.goal_clues: Safe tutorial: return from one-way switch to starting pad after shutter closes. Ghost trail and prompt show personal path.
puzzles.solution: Charge ≥25 EE, walk from pad through shutter to switch within 4 s, activate, press F to rewind to pad.
puzzles.result: World switch remains active; next door opens. Reset button restores shutter and gives EE, no progress loss.

puzzles.goal_clues: Reconstruct local connections. Three anchor panels show matching geometric halves and stable pulses.
puzzles.solution: Connect diamond A to A, split diamond B to B, ring C to C; follow resulting maintenance corridor.
puzzles.result: FIN01 accessible; wrong pair gives local mismatch. No extra powers.

puzzles.goal_clues: Three physical stabilizers on the western, upper and lower decks. Each reports readiness to Anchor Control. Warning: keep release path open.
puzzles.solution: Activate A/B/C in any order, open release line, energize receiver at Anchor Control.
puzzles.result: Final approach becomes stable. The physically broken transit interface remains broken.

puzzles.goal_clues: Power separate diagnostic channel after guardian defeated and gate inspected. Reserve source can route to broken transit or beacon.
puzzles.solution: Isolate transit load, connect reserve source to beacon receiver, confirm distress packet.
puzzles.result: Signal sent, refuge unlocked; invalid routing shows broken-interface warning. No player EE cost or gate repair.

bosses.name: Sluice Warden
bosses.moves: Maintenance construct; slam shockwave; double slam <50%; attack stuck arm/core.
bosses.counterplay: 1.0s wind-up; 1.4s recovery; phase chain 2 with clear pause. Safe mode opens bridge exit.

bosses.name: Mossbound Titan
bosses.moves: Root-covered maintenance guardian; root sweep, falling debris, expose side core.
bosses.counterplay: 0.9s tell; 1.3s recover; jump sweep, move from debris marker. MAP04 and alloy.

bosses.name: Wayfinder Colossus
bosses.moves: Damaged alignment construct; rear beam, ceiling marker, fold punch, resonance pulse.
bosses.counterplay: 0.8–1.2s warnings; 1.5s exposed core; all avoidable pre-Rewind. Phase2 combines two known attacks sequentially.

bosses.name: Reliquary Keeper
bosses.moves: Mithril vault guardian; paired conductors isolated first; shield pulses and core windows.
bosses.counterplay: Shield opens after pulse for 1.6s; dodge charge; short encounter. No Rewind required.

bosses.name: Rift Devourer
bosses.moves: Displaced Voruun predator; marked rift strike, delayed pool, charge.
bosses.counterplay: 1.0s tells; 1.5s recovery; use Rewind safely; HP04, MAP06, MEM05.

bosses.name: Fold Guardian / Last Custodian
bosses.moves: Containment system; Phase1 strikes/beams; Phase2 portal attacks; Phase3 delayed markers and exposed core.
bosses.counterplay: 1.0s minimum initial tell, 1.6s opening; phase thresholds 70%, 35%; no new last-second mechanic.
